title: fix(plugin-grid): the mobile card's amount line reads the field's own currency (objectui#10423)
body:
Fixes #10423
Clause-②: no

## What

`ObjectGrid`'s mobile card summarises the row's amount on one line. That line picked `amountCol` from the card's secondary columns and resolved its currency with `resolveFieldCurrency(amountCol as any, tenantCurrency)`. `amountCol` is a column draft (`accessorKey`, `header`, `type`, `cell`, ...), so it carries neither `currency` nor `currencyConfig`, and the line always fell through to the tenant currency. Under a USD tenant a JPY-fixed field read `¥1,234,567` in the desktop cell and `$1.2M` on the phone card of the same row.

The one-line fix resolves from the object schema's field def, `objectSchema?.fields?.[amountCol.accessorKey]`. That is the same lookup this card block already uses for its stage badge options (`resolveOptionMeta`), and the same def the desktop cell bags copy `currencyConfig` from since objectui#10354 (PR objectui#10418). Every column shape emits `accessorKey` as the field name (ListColumn objects: `accessorKey: col.field`; string columns and the inline `fields` projection: `accessorKey: fieldName`), so the lookup hits on all of them. The pin drives all three.

Only the amount line in the mobile card block changed. The fetch effect (objectui#10035) and the page-size reads (PR objectui#10278) are untouched.

## Pin

`packages/plugin-grid/src/__tests__/mobileCardFieldCurrency-10423.test.tsx` renders the real `ObjectGrid` at `innerWidth = 390` (the card layout; the test asserts that no `table` rendered) with a USD tenant. The field `amount` has `currencyConfig: { currencyMode: 'fixed', defaultCurrency: 'JPY' }`, and `classify` reads it as `amount`. The test waits for the schema-enriched card (the stage badge's option label `Won Label` comes off the fetched field defs), so a `$` read before the defs arrive cannot pass for the wrong reason. Each case runs on all three column shapes:

- JPY-fixed card line reads `¥1.2M`;
- control 1: `plain_amount` (no `currencyConfig`) still reads the tenant `$1.2M`;
- control 2: at `innerWidth = 1280` the desktop cell of the same fixture reads `¥1,234,567`.

Directions were predicted before the first run and observed as predicted. On the base tree `2a943bf0c`, the 3 JPY card cases went RED (`expected '$1.2M' to be '¥1.2M'`) and the 6 controls stayed GREEN. With the fix, 9/9 passed.

Reverse verification ran on the committed fix `c56ca5efe`. The fix line was mutated back to `resolveFieldCurrency(amountCol as any, tenantCurrency)` under a trap restore, confirmed on disk (fix anchor 1→0, draft anchor 0→1). Result: `Tests 3 failed | 6 passed (9)`, the same three RED. The file was then restored with `git checkout HEAD --`: `git diff HEAD` empty, blob hash equal to HEAD's. The test imports `../ObjectGrid` from source, so no dist rebuild sits between the mutation and the run.

## Gates (head `c56ca5efe`; the merge of `origin/main` before opening was a no-op, main had not moved from `2a943bf0c`)

- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-grid/`: `Test Files 155 passed (155)`, `Tests 1482 passed (1482)`, exit 0.
- `packages/plugin-grid` `type-check` (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`): exit 0, after building the dependency closure (`turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/plugin-grid^...'`, 13/13). `--listFiles` on `tsconfig.test.json` counts the new test file once.
- `eslint .` in `packages/plugin-grid`: 192 files (from `--format json`), 0 errors, exit 0. The new test file has 0 warnings, and there are none within 6 lines of the changed line.
- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` exit 0; `check-changeset-no-major` exit 0; `check:control-bytes` exit 0; `check:new-line-citations` `0 new citation(s)`; `check:test-path-roots` exit 0; `check:vi-mock-specifiers` exit 0.
- Repo-wide `pnpm lint` and the full `pnpm test` belong to CI.

## Acceptance notes

- Unprobed observation, not filed: the same card's percent line calls `formatPercent(value, undefined, displayLocale)`, while the desktop `PercentCellRenderer` reads the field's `scale ?? 0`. A percent field that declares `scale` may therefore show different decimals on the card than in the cell. It is not the draft-currency defect, and it was not measured here.
- The date lines in the card format with no field-def input on either face, so there is no draft-versus-def split for them.
